subject.title: Feature Request: Automated Session Memory Preservation & Synthesis

question: Should reset/startup memory synthesis be an OpenClaw core/default memory path, a plugin/MCP capability published through ClawHub, or only a narrowed plugin API gap?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the answer changes what OpenClaw persists by default, what it re-injects into prompts, which provider may process private transcript content, and whether this belongs in the special memory-plugin slot rather than core.

options.title: Keep Open For Core Memory Design
options.body: Keep this issue as the product/security packet and require a bounded design for synthesis, transcript receipts, redaction, retention, and startup hydration before implementation.

options.title: Route To Plugin Or ClawHub
options.body: Close only after maintainers decide reset synthesis is optional and current hook/plugin/MCP surfaces are sufficient for external packages such as `world-model-mcp`.

options.title: Narrow To API Gap
options.body: Split out only a missing hook or memory-plugin contract, then let memory plugins own synthesis policy and storage behavior.

recommendation.title: Keep Open For Core Memory Design
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the product/security packet and require a bounded design for synthesis, transcript receipts, redaction, retention, and startup hydration before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has the strongest recent history across session-memory sanitizer/release work and hooks documentation, and the decision touches that surface directly.
